transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in today?

Hi, yeah, thanks for seeing me. I guess what finally pushed me to make an appointment is that I just can’t seem to organize all the moving parts in my life anymore. 

I've got a lot of different things going on—patent notes, prep for workshops, gallery deadlines, team decisions at work—and I just can't seem to keep them sorted. Instead of tackling them in a way that makes sense, I end up just starting whatever is loudest or right in front of me, instead of focusing on what actually matters. It's just getting really hard to manage it all.
Have you noticed this kind of difficulty organizing and focusing on tasks going back to childhood or your school years, or is this something that started more recently?

Yeah, looking back, this was definitely there in grade school, too. Long before I was a teenager. 

My teachers used to write on my report cards that I was bright, but that I daydreamed a lot. I was constantly losing my homework folders, or... I'd actually do the work, finish an assignment, and then just completely forget to turn it in. So, yeah, it's not a recent thing at all, it's been around for a long time.
Growing up and even now, have you often felt restless, fidgety, or had trouble sitting still, or found yourself acting impulsively—like interrupting others or blurting things out?

I don't really have the impulsivity part—like, I'm not usually interrupting people or blurting things out. But the restlessness... yeah, definitely. 

Especially at work. Like, on long design calls, I... I start to feel this actual pressure building up in my body to just get up and move. So I end up pacing around my office, or I'll keep shifting from chair to chair, even when I’m on camera and really trying to look focused. It's just hard to stay planted in one spot for too long.

Would you say these organizational and focus difficulties are causing real problems not just at work, but also in other areas of your life—like at home, in relationships, or with personal responsibilities?

Honestly, the biggest hit has been at work. It's... it's actually starting to damage my reputation there, which is hard to admit. 

Like, I completely missed a checkpoint for a patent filing recently because I just lost track of it. And then I had a really difficult architecture review, and I struggled so much to keep all the details straight that my collaborators are... well, they're starting to question whether I can actually lead the larger project. So, yeah, it's causing some very real problems for me right now.
Can you recall specific examples from before age 12—like at home or in other settings outside school—where this disorganization or restlessness caused noticeable problems?

I'm not really sure about specific examples outside of school from back then. I mean, I remember the school stuff clearly because of the report cards and the lost homework, but... as for home or other places before I was 12, nothing specific is coming to mind right now. I just know it was always kind of a struggle to stay organized in general.
Have you been experiencing any low mood, anxiety, significant stress, sleep problems, or substance use that started around the same time as these concentration and restlessness issues?

No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed about work because of the things I mentioned—like the patent filing and the review—but I don't feel depressed or overly anxious in general. My sleep is fine, and I don't really drink much or use any substances. These focus issues and the restlessness... they've just kind of always been there, independent of my mood or anything else.
Outside of work, do you notice similar problems with disorganization or losing track of things—like at home, managing bills, appointments, or personal errands?

Yeah, I do. It's not just a work thing. At home, I'm... well, my desk is a mess of mail I haven't opened. I forget to pay bills on time pretty regularly unless they're on autopay, just because I put them down and completely forget they exist. And appointments... if I don't put it in my calendar the exact second I make it, I won't show up. I'll just double-book myself or completely blank on it. So, yeah, it definitely affects my personal life too.
